chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: The Lincoln Theatre, Billy Eckstine and Cecil Gant
summary: McGhee's big band at the Lincoln, and the crowd booing the Eckstine band because they wanted Private Cecil Gant.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And while we're still talking about Central Avenue, I'd like to mention about the Lincoln Theatre. Do you remember the Lincoln Theatre?

Yes, that's where they used to play all the top acts. I worked there with Howard McGhee with the big band that he assembled just for that date, that he and Gene Roland, the trombone player from Stan Kenton's band at the time, wrote all of the book.

But anyway, a funny thing happened. Sarah Vaughan... We have talked about it several times since that period. She came to Los Angeles with the Billy Eckstine band, and they played the Lincoln Theatre. Oh, that's when they had all the stars, you know, Dexter and Fats Navarro and everybody, Gene Ammons -- they had all the crew, you know. And, well, the people out here, they weren't really ready for that, you know. And there was a piano player and singer out here, and he was in the Army, called Private Cecil Gant. He had a big hit at the time on a song called 'I Wonder.' Do you remember that one?
[LAUGHS] Yeah, that was a real big... At that same time Ernie Andrews had 'Soothe Me,' about the same period, when he was sixteen years old; he had a big one, 'Soothe Me.'
But anyway, getting back to Cecil, Cecil was on the same bill with the Billy Eckstine Band at the Lincoln Theatre. And the people used to boo the band because they
wanted to hear Cecil sing 'I Wonder.' [LAUGHS] They was booing Sarah Vaughan and Billy Eckstine and Dizzy Gillespie and all of that. [LAUGHS] They had some pretty wild times.
